items.title: Iran's navy said an oil tanker caught fire on Saturday morning after hitting a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz, per Iranian state media; Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

Microsoft 365 services including Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams and Copilot suffered a global outage across Asia, Australia, the UK and the US; Microsoft said it saw no indication of malicious activity and had not named a root cause.

Enea reports SilentAir, a state-level actor abusing compromised Asian mobile-operator equipment and SS7 and Diameter signalling to divert calls and texts, mostly of Taiwanese targets, with 2FA codes intercepted after some diversions; Enea links it to China only with low confidence.

Europol-coordinated Operation Endgame took down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC infrastructure (235 servers, 257 domains per Europol) and the BKA reports about 6.4 million stolen logins from more than 40,000 victims; no arrests were announced, and the US Justice Department says Gootloader access fed ransomware attacks on at least 44 US victims with about $28.8 million in losses.
Huntback found an XMRig miner on 21 N-able N-central servers, 19 of them already on Hotfix 2, and N-able confirmed attackers are targeting customers that left the Legacy API enabled.

The Hacker News reports that UnrealIRCd CVE-2026-114713 (CVSS 8.6), fixed in 6.2.7.1 on 7 November, is exploited on the internet, with maintainer Bram Matthys saying attacks are under way and CISA listing it in KEV on 13 November.

The Hacker News, citing Check Point Research, reports that since 30 October attackers chained the PHP2Shell flaws with the Gaia root-escalation CVE-2026-123039 (CVSS 7.8) against a couple of dozen customers, installed the TSGA and TSProxy backdoors and in some Israeli cases pivoted to VMware ESXi to run a wiper; Check Point says it cannot tie the campaign to a China-nexus group.
CISA added UnrealIRCd CVE-2026-114713 (improper neutralization of delimiters) and Check Point multiple products CVE-2026-123039 (incorrect permission assignment) to the KEV catalog on 13 November.

Sudan's army and the allied Joint Force said they recaptured Al-Khuway and Sarif Ankoush in West Kordofan, claiming 20 RSF combat vehicles destroyed and 40 seized, while the RSF could not be reached for comment and the army separately said it downed a drone that entered Blue Nile from Ethiopia.

Critical Threats reports federal-TDF clashes near Rama, Gomahalo and Semema (about 20 miles south of Axum) between 7 and 11 November and an ENDF-Eritrean artillery exchange around Badme from 11 to 13 November, with ACLED saying neither side held Badme and Eritrea's information ministry accusing Ethiopia of invading on 12 November.

Ukrenergo scheduled all-day power cuts and strikes left consumers without power in 12 oblasts, with the Air Force counting 117 attack drones overnight and Zelenskyy saying Russia has hit energy facilities more than 310 times since the start of November.

The IRGC Navy said two oil tankers, including a supertanker, exploded and caught fire after hitting mines on an unauthorized route on Friday night, and warned ships to coordinate with its traffic-control centre; none of the IRGC claims have been independently verified.

Citrix patched 12 NetScaler and Secure Access Client flaws, including nine NetScaler memory overflows rated CVSS 9.3 to 9.5 and an unauthenticated authentication bypass in NetScaler Console (CVE-2026-120869, CVSS 9.4); Citrix says it knows of no exploits.

After two days of Abu Dhabi talks, US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Putin in Moscow and then Zelenskyy in Dublin; Witkoff said the trilateral format was restarted with a new meeting set, Zelenskyy said Europeans would join the next round and the biggest prisoner exchange of the war so far is planned, and no energy truce was reported.

Al Jazeera reports that after meeting US envoys Putin rejected any European troop presence in Ukraine, saying such forces would be legitimate targets, while Kremlin aide Ushakov said Putin will discuss Ukraine with Trump at the APEC summit later this month; the US and Russia agreed to resume direct talks after a nine-month pause, with no breakthrough reported from the Abu Dhabi round.

The UN Security Council voted unanimously to extend Yemen sanctions for one year and the mandate of its Panel of Experts, condemning Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and threats to shipping, Al Jazeera reports.

Al Jazeera reports that the Houthi spokesperson claimed drone and missile attacks on an East-West Pipeline pumping station, Yanbu, Sharurah airport, Khamis Mushait airbase and Aramco headquarters in Riyadh, while the coalition said it intercepted drones over the Riyadh region and Eastern Province; no independently confirmed damage was reported.

Fox News reports that Trump said he would not hesitate to strike Iran if it threatens US allies or ships in the strait, that Iran's Assembly of Experts called for a review of NPT membership and warned of a response without geographical limits, and that Brent settled at $95.82, up $3.06.

Iran's military said four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings about restricted areas, with two reported as hitting naval mines in the eastern strait; Reuters said it could not immediately verify the Iranian account.

The Justice Department said it obtained court-authorized seizure and restraint of more than $1.2 billion in assets stolen from Binance on about 29 October, that government and private-sector freezes exceed $2.7 billion, and that it seized infrastructure and more than 900 victim webcam videos in the FaceStealer campaign, which it says stole more than $400 million from crypto and Web3 workers over 18 months using deepfake video calls.

Cyprus Mail reports that the IMO has verified at least 130 attacks on commercial vessels in the region and at least 25 seafarer deaths since the conflict began, the latest after an attack on the tanker M/T VELOS SAPPHIRE in the Strait of Hormuz on 5 November, and that the IMO Council condemned Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait.
French Minister Delegate Haddad said the EU will adopt new sanctions on Monday targeting 150 additional entities and 50 banks (a minister's statement of intent, not yet adopted).

Al Jazeera reports that Kushner and Witkoff were meeting Putin in the Kremlin on 12 November after two days of US-mediated Abu Dhabi talks ended without a breakthrough; the US said differences remain on territory with some progress on post-war security guarantees, and a further prisoner exchange is planned.

Ukraine's General Staff said it has struck Russia's five largest oil refineries since 30 October (Omsk, Kirishi, Ryazan, Nizhny Novgorod and Yaroslavl) as well as the smaller Novokuibyshevsk and Saratov plants (party claim).

Ukraine's Deputy Energy Minister Nekrasov said overnight Russian strikes caused power outages in nine regions, Kyiv's mayor said a drone hit a residential block and killed one woman, and the military said it shot down 89 of 123 Russian combat drones (Ukrainian official claims).

G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris on 11 November expressed great concern over Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions and called for maximum restraint, as reported by Critical Threats; the same review notes five US Senate Democrats urged Rubio on 10 November to step up mediation.

Gunmen ambushed a police convoy bound for an illegal gold-mining site in Kohat district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killing eight police officers and wounding 13, a district official told AFP; no group claimed responsibility.

Fox News reports that UKMTO said a Liberian-flagged tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile about 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al-Khaimah, causing an engine-room fire and the evacuation of all 22 crew, and that a second tanker was struck by a projectile in the strait, with crew safe.

Iran's parliament speaker and chief negotiator Ghalibaf told Al Jazeera that Hormuz will not return to its pre-war status, that Iran and Oman agreed to oversee it, and that Tehran awaits a US reply, through a Qatari mediator, to seven conditions that include lifting the US naval blockade (party claims).

N-able released N-central 2026.4 HF2 fixing some of seven disclosed CVEs, including the most critical, after uncoordinated researcher disclosures on 8 November, and says all hosted servers are upgraded; Shadowserver counted about 148 exposed N-central servers, down from 1,338 a day earlier, and Defused saw probing, though N-able has not flagged exploitation.

Malbear Labs reports a Chinese-speaking actor used an autonomous framework built on a jailbroken DeepSeek Flash model to exploit Cisco BroadWorks CVE-2026-20320 against a European telecom provider and 13 organisations on its infrastructure; the attribution and the AI tooling come from Malbear alone.

Zelenskyy called the first day of the Abu Dhabi talks "constructive and quite substantive", covering humanitarian steps, prisoner exchanges, de-escalation and security guarantees, while Kushner called the meetings a "positive step" and Peskov said Moscow would give no details before the delegation briefed Putin (party statements).

Russian delegation head Medinsky said the two-day Abu Dhabi talks reached an agreement in principle on a new large-scale prisoner exchange, and RFE/RL reports that Witkoff and Kushner are due to meet Putin in Moscow on 12 November; no energy truce is mentioned (party claim).

Leningrad governor Drozdenko said several Ukrainian drones hit the Ust-Luga port area on the Baltic, starting a fire and injuring three workers, and Russia's Defence Ministry said it destroyed 627 Ukrainian drones overnight (Russian official claims; RFE/RL calls Ust-Luga Russia's largest Baltic energy and oil export hub).

Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 163 drones overnight into 11 November, 91 of them jet-powered, plus missiles, with impacts at 17 locations, and Prime Minister Koretskyi said six large substations were hit in Vinnytsia, Kirovohrad, Zhytomyr and Cherkasy (Ukrainian official claims).

Aikido and SafeDep report that 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts pushed a CI secret stealer into at least 8,093 repositories from 10 November, with test pull requests in 61,764 repositories; Aikido does not attribute it to the October GhostAction actor.

Vates confirmed exploitation of an authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra (advisory VSA-2026-062, no CVE yet) in which a crafted authenticationToken cookie holding an empty JSON object grants admin access; fixes ship in 6.9.1, 6.10.0 and xo-server 5.211.2 and 5.213.1.

Check Point Research links three China-nexus espionage clusters (SilentDelivery, OceanGate, DarkWire) to a shared Sparrow malware ecosystem built by a developer it codenames CopperDragon, serving five actors including FamousSparrow and Earth Estries; targets include telecom, government and military bodies in Latin America, Asia and Europe.
CISA added Cisco BroadWorks CVE-2026-20320, an unauthenticated XXE flaw in the OCI-P XML parser patched in August, to the KEV catalog on 10 November with a federal deadline of 24 November.

Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday fixed 1,235 flaws by BleepingComputer's count, including an Outlook spoofing zero-day, CVE-2026-124194, that Microsoft says is exploited: a crafted message file makes Outlook connect to an attacker-controlled location without the external-content warning and can expose NTLM hashes.

Bloomberg copy reports Eurasia Group cut its odds of renewed all-out US-Iran hostilities to 30% from 60% after Trump said further strikes were not necessary; Brent fell 1.6% in early trading to $91.10 (its lowest closing level since August), Tehran wants the US blockade lifted before talks and Washington presses Iran to stop attacking shipping immediately.
ESET documents Turla's modular Cereal toolset on Exchange servers at a Kazakh government body and a Romanian agency, where it collected mail exchanged with NATO and EU officials.
Barracuda says CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560 in its Email Security Gateway are exploited against a small number of organisations.
US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks begin in Abu Dhabi, headline
The Houthi health ministry said a Saudi strike on a gas facility in Sanaa killed one person and wounded three.
The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis at Riyadh early on 10 November, and AFP journalists heard several blasts and residents received shelter alerts.
Ukrainian police detained four members of a pig-butchering ring that took over EUR 4.3 million from 135 German victims, working with German law enforcement.
NoName057(16) published personal data on 18 European officials, police and journalists and offered crypto rewards for more.
The BYOD ransomware gang claims the Vanderbilt University attack and over 1 million SSNs; the university has not confirmed ransomware or data theft.
A seller using the ShinyHunters name offers 335 million alleged Binance user records for $900,000; Binance finds no breach and calls it a likely scam.
France attributes the October attacks on Danfoss refrigeration controllers, about 700 retail sites and at least 15 fires, to IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh.
Fireworks AI disclosed a second breach, reached through a third-party cloud provider on 23-24 October, and engaged Unit 42.
N-able took hosted N-central offline after a researcher published more than 30 alleged zero-days with proof-of-concept code, with no exploitation seen so far.
CISA adds GPUStack, SignalWire FreeSWITCH, OpenSSH and IBM Aspera Faspex flaws to the KEV catalog.
The Independent reports Elliptic's 9 November analysis that TraderTraitor is minting novelty memecoins to obscure the $6.3bn Binance proceeds, about $430,000 of which has passed through them so far.
Estonian Interior Minister Igor Taro told the Financial Times Russian acts in Europe should be called state terrorism, linking the August Milrem Robotics arson to Russia-recruited suspects.
Leningrad governor Drozdenko said air defences downed 113 Ukrainian drones overnight and one person was injured at an industrial site in Kirishi.

Overnight Russian and Ukrainian strikes on 8-9 November left more than 600,000 without power in Dnipropetrovsk region and about 250,000 customers in Kharkiv, per DTEK and local figures relayed by SANA.
EEPA reports the ENDF mobilised thousands of additional troops to the Sheraro and Rama front, with control of Rama disputed between the TPLF and ACLED-cited accounts.
Lebanon's Janoubia portal, relayed by APA, reported Israeli air strikes on at least five southern villages, drone strikes and artillery fire, with residents injured and no figure given.
Araghchi outlined a sequence in which the US acts on day one and Hormuz reopens on day two, while Rubio said talks have made no progress and called Iran's demands unrealistic.
Brent fell over 1% to $91.56 near 10-week lows on 10 November, and Trump said after meeting Qatar's prime minister that new strikes were quite unlikely and the war could end fairly soon.

Hormozgan's deputy governor said overnight US strikes hit Qeshm island without damaging residential or vital infrastructure, Rubio repeated that such strikes are defensive, and Trump said 38 bridges are marked if the war restarts at scale.
Iranian state television said 11 tankers have been attacked over the past 10 days with four unable to continue transit, and the IRGC rejected the US claim that all mines are cleared.

A Saudi energy ministry official told SPA the East-West pipeline in Medina region was struck on 9 November, causing a limited fire that was put out with operations unaffected; the article does not name who carried out the strike.

Help Net Security reports Credit Mutuel Arkea declined to confirm the EUR 118 million estimate beyond an order of magnitude, said part of the funds were blocked, and denied entry via Fortuneo; ZachXBT says laundering indicators make Lazarus unlikely and that OTC activity may put losses above $133 million

CNBC reports that authorities have not identified who is behind the refrigeration tampering at Ahold Delhaize, IKEA, Colruyt and Carrefour sites in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden and the Netherlands, that the Kremlin called suggestions of Russian involvement baseless, and that analysts split between a state actor and boundary testing

CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT warn that actors are targeting internet-exposed industrial refrigeration and cold-chain controllers worldwide; The Hacker News reports hundreds of supermarkets in 12 European countries hit, setpoints raised to as high as 50C, three French Blood Establishment plasma storage sites affected through a refrigeration provider, and no attribution; Censys saw Danfoss StoreView exposure fall from 3,004 to 708 instances between 9 October and 5 November
Attackers hit a police checkpoint on Shah Almas Pir Mountain in Hangu district, killing one policeman and abducting three; no group was named and a search operation is under way

Zelenskyy said the EU agreed a fund to speed grid repairs, and Trump told "60 Minutes" the sides are "very close" to a deal ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks starting Tuesday; AP notes Geneva in February produced no significant progress
Leningrad governor Drozdenko said Ukrainian drones started a fire at the KINEF refinery at Kirishi, which AP places more than 1,200 km from the border

AP reports Ukraine's air force counted 317 Russian drones overnight into 9 November, 105 of them jet-powered, while Russia's Defence Ministry said it struck four electrical substations in the Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Cherkasy and Vinnytsia regions; the Russian figure is a party claim
The White House said Task Force Iron Gate is operating with full force and effect, Trump said very little gets into or out of Iran, and the IRGC dismissed the expanded blockade as a play on words.
Iranian state TV reported three projectiles launched from Sirik toward the Strait of Hormuz and explosions were heard on Qeshm Island; the causes remain unconfirmed.
Malay Mail (AFP wire) reports Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh were intercepted by the Saudi-led coalition while witnesses reported damage to an Aramco tower in the financial district, headline
The Revolutionary Guard said it lifted its self-imposed 2,000 kilometre limit on ballistic missile range, as relayed by ABC

The Associated Press reports Iran is reviewing Qatari proposals on its nuclear programme and Trump spoke with Qatar's emir on 6 November; an Iranian official said Tehran will not negotiate its atomic activities until the US meets several conditions
US Central Command said one of its aircraft disabled a St Kitts-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman after it ignored warnings and tried to leave the region after visiting an Iranian port
Iran's military said two tankers caught fire after hitting mines on an "unauthorised route" through the strait; ABC reports no independent confirmation
Acting President Ana Brnabic announced that Serbia's new National Assembly will hold its constitutive session on 17 November at 10:00, after which parliament has up to 90 days to elect a government.

Anadolu, citing army statements and military sources, reports air defences downed an FH-95 drone east of Wad Banda on 7 November without naming its operator, and that RSF vehicles were destroyed near Al-Khuwei.

The Sudanese army said it captured Ayal Bakhit and Umm Marahik northwest of Al-Khuwei and shot down a fourth drone in West Kordofan within a week, while the Joint Force reported a third day of offensive operations.

Militants raided the Shah Almas Pir Pahari checkpost in Hangu late on Sunday and killed one policeman, and the three abducted officers were later recovered unharmed through joint efforts of police, tribal elders and the district administration.
President Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, with 28 days and a possible two-week extension, after neither bloc won a majority on 27 October.
The IRGC said it struck three tankers for using unauthorised routes in coordination with the US military, and a tanker was reported on fire near Hormuz; the report cites no outside confirmation.
Saudi officials said falling debris from an attempted attack damaged several floors of the Aramco Tower in Riyadh, with SPA images showing officials inspecting it.
The Houthis said on 8 November that they attacked Riyadh's business district, a claim AFP relays without independent confirmation.
A policeman was shot dead in Tank district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and his son wounded; Governor Faisal Karim Kundi blamed the TTP

ISW cites the Ukrainian Air Force for 164 Russian strike drones (112 jet-powered) and three cruise missiles overnight into 8 November, with outages in six oblasts and power restrictions in Kyiv City and about 600,000 people without power in Dnipro city and Dnipropetrovsk Oblast

President Herzog formally tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming Israel's next government after the 27 October vote left his four-party alliance on 48 seats and Netanyahu's bloc on 53, short of 61; Eisenkot said he is open to Netanyahu joining
The UAE National Guard Coast Guard rescued all 22 crew of a cargo ship that caught fire in the Gulf of Oman; all were in stable condition and the cause was not stated.

Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said mediators stopped travelling after the US midterms, Secretary of State Rubio said the sides are not on the verge of a breakthrough, and Trump said renewed strikes are highly unlikely if talks progress.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed six operations against targets in Saudi Arabia and Yemen, including King Khalid airport, Aramco storage and the financial centre in Riyadh, Khurais, Abqaiq and Pumping Station No. 8 in Dawadmi; the group later described four operations, and the claims are uncorroborated.

The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired toward Riyadh and later two cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh and the southern region; Saudi Energy Ministry said shrapnel caused minor damage to an Aramco administrative building in Riyadh with no injuries.

Trilateral talks are scheduled for 10 and 11 November in Abu Dhabi; Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Zakharova called any foreign deployment to Ukraine "categorically unacceptable" and said Europeans have no place at the talks
ISW describes the Ukrainian strike on the Saratov oil refinery on the night of 6 to 7 November as at least the eighth against it in 2026, citing Russian and Ukrainian reporting

ISW counted 172 Russian drones, 137 of them jet-powered, in the overnight raid into 7 November; Zelensky said Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv city and oblast and that a substation linking the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants to Kyiv was damaged

Trump called new US strikes on an Iranian air defence system on 6 November "minor" and said he is weighing a further wave after the 3 November midterms; the US launched Task Force Iron Gate on 7 November to curb Iranian movement of advanced weapons and sanctioned materials
Iran's navy, via IRNA, said a tanker caught fire after hitting a sea mine east of the strait; the Straits Live brief notes no maritime authority has confirmed it

gCaptain reported one seafarer killed in a suspected missile attack on the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Velos Sapphire, sailing unladen toward Bahrain, as relayed in the Straits Live daily brief, headline
The Saudi-led coalition spokesman said air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi cruise missile launched toward the Riyadh region on 7 November, in a statement relayed by Anadolu
GreyNoise logged the first successful in-the-wild exploitation of the OpenSSH SSHole bypass (CVE-2026-123158) on 7 November, 16 chains from six IPs.

Elliptic traced about 117,000 NEAR (roughly $430,000) of Binance loot through six newly created memecoins between 5 and 7 November, with about $2.85 billion frozen or seized and about $3 billion still in linked addresses.
KBA13 reports six killed in the 7 November Krakow shooting and assesses the attacker as a self-radicalised individual, with no public evidence of foreign direction.

A company security officer told UKMTO a vessel was hit by a projectile on an outbound Hormuz transit with crew safe, open-source analysts tentatively identified a burning tanker off Khasab as the Navig8 Messi, and CENTCOM said US forces disabled the bulker Huda.
CENTCOM announced Task Force Iron Gate to block Iranian overland arms and goods flows and said enforcement since July redirected 147 commercial vessels while five that refused were disabled.

Misbar used satellite imagery to identify probable damage at four power substations (Shendi, Al-Dabba, Al-Rawma, New Halfa) and reports drone attacks on 17 substations across 10 states within a week; the government blames the RSF

Reuters reported that Russia's overnight raid on 7 November hit energy sites around Kyiv, seriously damaged lines carrying power from two nuclear plants and damaged the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro, killing at least two and wounding about a dozen, with Zelenskiy saying only four of 36 ballistic missiles were intercepted

Lebanon's state news agency, cited by Anadolu, reported an Israeli demolition operation in Bani Hayyan, search operations in Khiam and artillery and machine-gun fire on Wadi al-Hujair, Baraachit, Mansouri and Bayut al-Sayyad, while the health ministry put deaths from Israeli attacks since 2 March at 4,390 as of 5 November

Anadolu, citing unnamed military sources, reports the Sudanese army and the Joint Force took Ayyal Bakhit in West Kordofan on 7 November and says fighting across North, West and South Kordofan has intensified since 25 October

QNAP said it has multiple reports of NAS devices compromised through the Plex2Shell chain (CVE-2026-96652, -96654, -96655, -96656) in Plex Media Server, exploited after technical details appeared on 16 October and listed in KEV on 20 October; it advises treating exposed devices as compromised and updating to Plex 1.43.3.10861
CISA's KEV catalog lists SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN CVE-2026-19868 (added 6 November), Apple CVE-2024-27834 (4 November) and WordPress Core CVE-2026-119977 (3 November) as the newest additions

SonicWall disclosed CVE-2026-19868, an SSL-VPN authentication bypass (CVSS 7.1) in SonicOS configurations using SAML that can defeat SAML-enforced MFA, and said its PSIRT investigated a report of potential exploitation; CISA listed it in KEV with a 20 November federal deadline; fixed in 7.3.4-7013 and 8.2.3-8015, no workaround

ISW reported that an unidentified actor sent hoax bomb threats to at least 18 commercial flights and airports on 6 November and more than 50 threats to European aviation that week; no explosives were found and no state has attributed the campaign

ISW assessed that Russia launched 227 drones, 86 of them jet-powered, at Ukraine overnight into 6 November, with Ukrenergo reporting new outages, and that geolocated footage shows a smoke plume at the Afipsky refinery, at least the sixth Ukrainian strike on it in 2026

The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched toward Najran and a drone over the Makkah region on 6 November; debris fell at Najran with damage under assessment, and the coalition did not attribute the drone

Russia's Defence Ministry said it intercepted 142 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea overnight into 6 November; Krasnodar authorities reported a fire at an industrial site in Afipsky, which Astra identified as the Afipsky oil refinery, about 3% of Russian refining capacity

Ukraine's General Staff said it shot down or jammed 196 Russian drones overnight into 6 November, with impacts or debris at 22 locations, and the Moscow Times reports outages across seven regions including Kyiv and Kharkiv, with the capital region's grid partly shut after heavy damage
FinCEN ordered MEXC cut off from the US financial system, citing at least $16 billion in illicit flows tied to cybercrime and Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion.
QNAP reports user compromises of NAS devices through the four-flaw Plex2Shell chain in Plex Media Server.
Newsrooms at Ireland's RTE and Bulgaria's Nova TV received emailed bomb threats signed 'Mikhail Andropov', and RTE evacuated and suspended programming; Reuters could not verify the sender.

The Hacker News reports, in an update of 8 November, exploitation of OpenSSH 'SSHole' (CVE-2026-123158, CVSS 8.1) on musl-based Linux such as Alpine with PAM disabled: Previdian saw the first attempt under nine hours after the CVE was published and root on a honeypot, and 20 attempts from 13 IPs by 8 November; fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2; no KEV listing is mentioned

Sekoia attributes to APT29 a campaign using patched iOS and Android browser flaws and the DarkSword toolkit against devices in Ukraine, the US and Europe, delivered through compromised sites and a Ukrainian analytics script (Plerdy); the targets included a Ukrainian gas producer and a US chemical trade association
CISA and US government partners published a fact sheet urging hardening of industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems on 5 November

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree denied the coalition's 5 November announcement that it destroyed a ballistic missile fired toward Madinah and claimed 61 Saudi air raids in the previous 24 hours; neither account is independently verified

Pakistani security sources, relayed by Radio Pakistan, said forces foiled a TTP infiltration attempt in Kurram's Shaluzan sector on 5 November and heavily damaged Afghan Taliban posts after what they called unprovoked Taliban fire; no casualties were reported and the Taliban have not replied

The Guards and the Iranian army said at least five tankers and a tugboat caught fire after hitting mines east and south of the Strait of Hormuz on 5 November; Al Jazeera could not confirm the incidents and the counts differ between the two Iranian accounts
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile fired toward the Medina region, after Saudi civil defence issued an alert for Yanbu Governorate

AFP reports that Machado endorsed a US State Department roadmap under which interim president Rodriguez would declare the presidency vacant and call elections within six months, with the Supreme Court renewed before end-2026 and a new electoral council immediately after; Rodriguez has given no date.
A former FBI supervisory special agent pleaded guilty to moving about $2.47 million in crypto out of wallets tied to 35 FBI cases.
Hoax bomb threats disrupted more than two dozen European flights on Thursday and prompted fighter escorts, with no government formally naming a culprit for the threats, Reuters reports.
Eritrea's UN envoy conditioned dialogue on Ethiopia renouncing force on 4 November, and Ethiopian State Minister Hadera Abera accused Eritrea of continued incursions on 5 November.

The Hacker News ThreatsDay reports Kaspersky saw an extortion-only PAYLOAD attack on a Middle Eastern manufacturer via a malicious Group Policy Object, and Check Point found HYFLOCK encrypts only the first 4,096 bytes of some files and lists 13 victims

Serbia's electoral commission declared final results giving the Students' List 140 of 250 seats and Vucic's SNS 103, with the inaugural session due within 30 days; nine police officers were detained on 4 November over alleged abuse of students
CISA added Apple CVE-2024-27834, an improper authentication flaw in multiple Apple products, to the KEV catalog on 4 November

Ethiopia ordered six Sudanese diplomats to leave, including staff of the Assosa consulate within 48 hours, and Sudan closed Ethiopia's consulate in Gedaref within hours, per unnamed officials; neither foreign ministry issued a statement

Al Jazeera, relaying The New York Times, reports unnamed Pentagon officials and commanders saying US forces are poised to resume major combat operations against Iran on Trump's order; the article confirms no decision

UKMTO reported that a tanker was hit by two projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash-Shamal, Qatar, at 2320 GMT on 4 November; the vessel was not identified and no one claimed the attack

Brent fell $8.94, or 8.6%, to $94.66 a barrel at 1:06 p.m. ET on 4 November, its lowest since 4 September and down from near $118 the previous Friday, as traders priced an end to the war after the US midterms; an unnamed senior Iranian official dismissed reports of progress in US-Iran talks

South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said North Korea fired several missiles from the Sondok area toward the Sea of Japan, the fourth DPRK weapons launch in a month; Pyongyang called the FBI's Binance attribution "a trite provocation" and Kim Yo Jong ruled out talks with Washington

Russia launched 310 long-range drones overnight into 4 November, 272 of them intercepted per the Air Force; attacks over the past day killed six and injured 50, energy sites were hit in six regions and emergency outages were introduced in Kyiv and other regions

The Houthis claimed drone and ballistic missile attacks on an airport and an airbase in southwestern Saudi Arabia; coalition spokesman Turki Al Maliki said three drones were intercepted over the Mecca region, the Eastern Province and the south
The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump leaned toward a large attack on Iran after the midterms but had not decided; the US has not confirmed an attack plan
President Trump told Fox News the US must do "something large" about Iran, which could include a "heavy hit", and confirmed US strikes on Qeshm Island as a "minor attack" on an anti-aircraft facility
The Revolutionary Guards said four "non-compliant" oil tankers were destroyed by naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz and were still burning, and that two other vessels had been halted

mSeven Software told mSecure customers on 3 November to change passwords, reset 2FA and remove passkeys after customers reported theft of an encrypted mSecure Cloud database; the company has not said how the breach occurred or how many users are affected
KCNA said North Korea test-fired a newly designed air-defense missile system on 4 November and that a separate firepower subunit conducted a fire strike, calling both obligatory military activities

The RSF and SPLM-N said they took the Sali military base in Blue Nile state, which the army did not answer; the army said its air defences downed a hostile drone that crossed from Ethiopia without naming the operator

UKMTO said a tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles, both hitting the engine room, about 14 nautical miles northeast of Limah off Oman at 1900 GMT on 3 November; no casualties or environmental damage were reported and the source was not identified

The Hacker News reports CISA added the WordPress Core race condition CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS 8.1) to KEV with a federal fix deadline of 6 November, and Wordfence counted more than 18,500 requests to staged installer paths in the first 21 hours after disclosure

Binance's incident report describes the 29 October theft as the end of a campaign that began with a malicious Homebrew install in June, continued through fake recruiter interviews and a malware "assignment" repository in September, reached wallet engineers on 20 October and used a stolen container deployment token on 29 October; the FBI attributes it to TraderTraitor
